note: The Rulebook — follow these every time you make a short. AI-generated from our data + research; the AI adds/updates rules as we learn. Trust: ✅ validated = holds out-of-sample (LOO) · 🟡 directional = real but small-n / unproven · 🔵 craft = sound judgment, not yet in the stats.

stages.title: The intro — wins the SWIPE
stages.sub: Decided in ~1 second. The opening VISUAL is everything; words barely matter here.

stages.title: The body — wins WATCH-THROUGH (AVD)
stages.sub: What keeps them after the swipe. Audio + pacing + script.

stages.title: Topic — wins VIEWS
stages.sub: Views = topic + reach + luck, NOT opening craft.

stages.title: Craft notes
stages.sub: Sound practice that hasn't earned a coefficient yet.

rules.rule: Every intro MUST have all four

items.label: Something INTERESTING / novel — a "what is that?!" mystery

rules.why: These are the four levers that stop the scroll. A face is validated (ρ+0.78); contrast is craft; early action and a novel/mysterious subject are directional. If an opening is missing any one, fix it before anything else.

rules.rule: Put a clear FACE in the first frame.
rules.why: Strongest swipe driver: ρ+0.78 (short bucket, n=11). Shorts with a face in frame 1 average ~74% stayed vs ~63% without.

rules.rule: Open on a MYSTERY — let them wonder "what is that?" Don't explain or label the object up front.
rules.why: Low object-clarity drives the swipe (ρ−0.73). Counter-example we caught: the floating-pot version with the plant already in it explained the object and scored lower than the bare floating pot.

rules.rule: Lead frame 1 with the cool thing ALREADY happening (the float, the glow, the arc) — never an inert/off object or a slow setup.
rules.why: The plasma re-edit gained +12.6 pts stayed by opening on the glowing ball instead of the off one. Put the payoff on frame 1.

rules.rule: Use quick CUTS in the first 4s (3+), and land the first cut/zoom before 0.5s — no static first second.
rules.why: Cuts in the first 4s: ρ+0.65. A slow/static opening second is a stall risk that bleeds the swipe.

rules.rule: NEVER narrate a "nothing's happening" / "it seems like nothing happens" line in the open.
rules.why: The clearest swipe-killer in the words analysis — and the 100-video competitor set agrees: top openings have ~0% dead-air.

rules.rule: Open LOUD and energetic — and NEVER ramp the loudness UP later.
rules.why: The AVD model: AVD ≈ 90.25 − 134·audio_buildup. Front-loaded loudness wins; ramping up tanks watch-through. (±2.1, most reliable model we have.)

rules.rule: Open with a STATEMENT, not a question.
rules.why: Questions ('does this actually work?') consistently underperform. Switching the phone-AC open from a question to a statement was the core fix.

rules.rule: Lead with an against-the-norm or stakes line ("I thought… but…", or a price like "$100").
rules.why: On the floating pot, the '$100 / I thought it was just two magnets' hook beat the dry 'if you take a sensor and electromagnet…' explainer.

rules.rule: Keep it SHORT — the shortest length that lands the hook + one clear payoff (single-object demo ≈ 20–25s).
rules.why: Shortening a 38s cut to ~22s lifted AVD. Rules differ by length bucket; short videos retain best.

rules.rule: To grow VIEWS, choose the FORMAT/topic — comparison/versus & knockoff tests beat single-object demos (~23×).
rules.why: Topic sets the view ceiling. Confirmed on 100 competitor videos: 'versus' formats out-viewed single-object demos ~23×.

rules.rule: Don't expect a better intro to grow VIEWS — opening craft drives the SWIPE and watch-through, not views.
rules.why: No opening/script feature predicts views (ours or 100 competitors'). Views = topic + channel reach + luck.
Competitor top-view openings are brighter & clearer, but brightness isn't a proven swipe lever in our own data — treat as craft, don't over-tweak.
